messages.content: What was MGIC Investment Corporation's PMIERs Available Assets and excess over Minimum Required Assets at December 31, 2024?
MGIC's PMIERs Available Assets totaled **$5.8 billion** at December 31, 2024, with an excess of **$2.2 billion** over its Minimum Required Assets (MTG, FY2024 10-K).
How did Radian Group's primary mortgage insurance in force change from December 31, 2023 to December 31, 2024?
Radian Group's primary mortgage insurance in force (IIF) was **$270.0 billion** at December 31, 2023, and **$275.1 billion** at December 31, 2024 — an increase of **$5.1 billion** (RDN, FY2024 10-K).
What was Essent Group's new insurance written (NIW) for the year ended December 31, 2024?
Essent Group's new insurance written (NIW) for the year ended December 31, 2024 was approximately **$45.6 billion** (ESNT, FY 2024 10-K).
What was NMI Holdings' annualized persistency rate at December 31, 2024, and how did it compare to year-end 2023?

NMI Holdings' annual persistency was **85% at December 31, 2024**, compared to **86% at December 31, 2023** — a decline of 1 percentage point year-over-year. Management noted persistency remained "historically high due to a continued slowdown in the pace of mortgage refinancing activity tied to the prevailing interest and mortgage rate environment" (NMIH 10-K, FY2024).
In its FY2024 10-K, did MGIC report favorable or unfavorable prior-year loss reserve development on previously received delinquency notices? Approximately what was the dollar amount?

Yes — MGIC reported **favorable** prior-year loss reserve development on previously received delinquency notices in its FY2024 10-K. The amount was approximately **$212.5 million** ($212,476 thousand), driven primarily by a decrease in the expected claim rate on existing delinquencies as home price appreciation allowed more borrowers to cure through property sales (MTG, FY2024 10-K, MD&A and Note 8).
What were NMI Holdings' three largest states by primary risk in force concentration at December 31, 2024?

As of December 31, 2024, NMI Holdings' three largest states by primary risk in force (RIF) concentration were:

1. **California** – 10.1%
2. **Texas** – 8.6%
3. **Florida** – 7.3%

(NMIH 10-K, FY 2024, Geographic Dispersion table)
What was Arch Capital Group's mortgage insurance subsidiaries' PMIERs Sufficiency Ratio at December 31, 2024, and how did it change from year-end 2023?

At December 31, 2024, Arch Capital's eligible mortgage insurance subsidiaries (Arch Mortgage Insurance Company and United Guaranty Residential Insurance Company) reported a **PMIERs sufficiency ratio of 186%**, down from **213%** at December 31, 2023 (ACGL 10-K 2024, p. 90). That's a decline of 27 percentage points year-over-year.

The filing also notes that if the August 2024 PMIERs update (which adds new deductions to available assets for investment risk, effective March 31, 2025 with phase-in through September 2026) had been fully implemented at year-end 2024, the pro-forma sufficiency ratio would have been approximately **154%**.
Did Arch Capital Group repurchase common shares in fiscal year 2024? Approximately how much?

Yes, Arch Capital Group repurchased common shares in fiscal year 2024, but the amount was modest — **$23.5 million** for **0.3 million shares** at an average price of $89.65 per share (ACGL, FY 2024 10-K). The company's larger capital-return action in 2024 was a special cash dividend of $1.9 billion ($5.00 per share). This contrasts sharply with FY 2025, when Arch repurchased $1.9 billion worth of stock.
Did Enact Holdings pay a special dividend during 2024, and what was its regular quarterly common-stock dividend rate at year-end 2024?

**No special dividend in 2024.** Enact paid special dividends of $0.71/share (Q4 2023) and $1.12/share (Q4 2022), but in 2024 all four quarterly payments ($0.16 in Q1, then $0.185 in Q2–Q4) were regular dividends only — no special component (ACT_10-K_2024-12-31, Item 5 and Note 13).

**Regular quarterly dividend rate at year-end 2024: $0.185 per share.** The board increased the quarterly rate from $0.16 to $0.185 effective with the Q2 2024 payment, and that $0.185 rate remained in place for Q3 2024, Q4 2024, and the Q1 2025 dividend declared in February 2025 (ACT_10-K_2024-12-31, "Dividends" section under Item 5 and "Capital returns" in MD&A).
In its FY2024 10-K, what does Arch Capital identify as the expected impact of the August 2024 GSE updates to PMIERs on its mortgage insurance subsidiaries' available assets and Sufficiency Ratio?

In its FY2024 10-K (ACGL_10-K_2024-12-31), Arch Capital identifies that if PMIERs Guidance 2024-01 (the August 2024 GSE updates) were fully phased in at year-end 2024, it would result in a **17% reduction to Available Assets** across its eligible mortgage insurance subsidiaries (AMIC and UGRIC). The pro-forma PMIERs **sufficiency ratio** under full phase-in would have been approximately **154%**, compared to the actual reported sufficiency of **186%** as of December 31, 2024.
What was MGIC's new insurance written (NIW) in Q3 2024, and how did it compare to Q2 2024?
MGIC's new insurance written (NIW) was **$17.2 billion** in Q3 2024, up from **$13.5 billion** in Q2 2024 — a sequential increase of **$3.7 billion, or ~27%**.
What was Essent Group's primary insurance in force at March 31, 2025, and how did it change from December 31, 2024?

At March 31, 2025, Essent Group's primary insurance in force (IIF) was **$244.7 billion**, up from $243.6 billion at December 31, 2024 — an increase of approximately **$1.0 billion** (ESNT, Q1 2025 10-Q).
What were Radian Guaranty's PMIERs Available Assets and PMIERs Excess Available Assets at March 31, 2025?

At March 31, 2025, Radian Guaranty's PMIERs **Available Assets** were **$6.0 billion**, and its **PMIERs Cushion** (excess available assets over minimum required assets) was **$2.1 billion** (53% above Minimum Required Assets). (RDN, Q1 2025 10-Q)

At year-end 2024, what was the dispersion in PMIERs sufficiency ratios across the six MI cohort issuers — which had the highest, which had the lowest, and what was the spread?

At year-end 2024, PMIERs sufficiency ratios across the six MI issuers were:

| MI | Sufficiency Ratio (Available ÷ Required) |
|---|---|
| **Arch** (USMI) | **186%** ← highest |
| Essent | 178% |
| NMI Holdings | ~170%* |
| Enact | 167% |
| MGIC | ~161% |
| **Radian** | **~156%** ← lowest |

*NMI reports on an (excess ÷ required) basis; 70% excess/required ≈ 170% on the available/required basis used by the others.

**Highest:** Arch Capital's eligible mortgage insurers at **186%** (ACGL_10-K_2024-12-31).

**Lowest:** Radian Guaranty at **~156%** (disclosed a $2.2B cushion "or 56% over Minimum Required Assets," implying MRA ~$3.85B against $6.0B Available; RDN_10-K_2024-12-31).

**Spread:** approximately **30 percentage points** (186% − 156%).

After the August 2024 PMIERs update revising Available Asset credit factors, which MI cohort issuer disclosed the largest pro-forma reduction to its YE 2024 PMIERs sufficiency ratio if the update were fully effective immediately, and how does it compare to the other five issuers' disclosures?

## Facts retrieved

- **Arch (ACGL):** YE 2024 PMIERs sufficiency ratio of 186%; pro-forma if Guidance 2024-01 fully phased in immediately would be 154% (a reduction of 32 percentage points, with Available Assets reduced by 17%) (ACGL_10-K_2024-12-31)
- **MGIC (MTG):** YE 2024 PMIERs sufficiency ratio of ~161% (Available Assets $5.8B, excess $2.2B); pro-forma if Guidance 2024-01 fully phased in immediately would reduce Available Assets by ~1% or $50M, resulting in excess of $2.1B (MTG_10-K_2024-12-31)
- **Essent (ESNT):** YE 2024 PMIERs sufficiency ratio of 178% (Available Assets $3.6B, Minimum Required Assets $2.0B); no pro-forma reduction disclosed; Essent states the update "will have no impact on Essent's Available Assets or sufficiency ratio until March 31, 2025" (ESNT_10-K_2024-12-31)
- **Enact (ACT):** YE 2024 PMIERs sufficiency ratio of 167% (Available Assets $5,095M, Net Required Assets $3,043M); no pro-forma reduction disclosed; Enact states it "does not expect the impact of these updates to be material to our sufficiency" (ACT_10-K_2024-12-31)
- **Radian (RDN):** YE 2024 PMIERs sufficiency ratio of ~156% (Available Assets $6.0B, Cushion $2.2B, implied MRA ~$3.85B); no pro-forma reduction disclosed; Radian states it "does not expect the PMIERs Updates to have a material impact on Radian Guaranty's capital position, its PMIERs Cushion or its investment portfolio asset allocation strategy" (RDN_10-K_2024-12-31)
- **NMI (NMIH):** YE 2024 PMIERs sufficiency ratio of ~170% on Available÷Required basis (Available Assets $3,108M, Net Required Assets $1,829M); no pro-forma reduction disclosed; NMI states it "does not expect the updated PMIERs to have a material impact on our available assets and risk-based required assets" (NMIH_10-K_2024-12-31)

According to the GSEs' August 2024 PMIERs update (Guidance 2024-01), what is the implementation phase-in schedule, and what substantive change does it make to the PMIERs standards?

Guidance 2024-01 (issued August 21, 2024, effective March 31, 2025) makes two changes:

**Substantive change.** It tightens Section 703's definition of Available Assets by: requiring all bonds to be rated (by S&P, Moody's, Fitch, A.M. Best, DBRS, or KBRA) — unrated bonds are ineligible; introducing a graded haircut table by rating (0.20% for AAA up to 100% for CCC+ and below); excluding mortgage insurance-linked notes, all non-agency RMBS, and bonds below specified rating/term thresholds; raising the discount on common/preferred shares from 25% to 50%; and adding new concentration limits (GSE debt/MBS ≤ 25% of Available Assets, ABS ≤ 20%, sub-investment-grade bonds + common/preferred shares aggregate ≤ 5%, non-agency CMBS ≤ 5%, eligible surplus notes capped at 9% of Minimum Required Assets, COLI ≤ 10% of risk-based required asset amount).

**Phase-in schedule.** The new rules phase in over six quarters:

| Quarter ending | Add-back of prior framework | Implied phase-in of new rules |
|---|---|---|
| March 31, 2025 & June 30, 2025 | 75% | 25% |
| September 30, 2025 & December 31, 2025 | 50% | 50% |
| March 31, 2026 & June 30, 2026 | 25% | 75% |
| September 30, 2026 onward | 0% | 100% |

*(Source: INDUSTRY_PMIERS_GUIDANCE_2024-01)*
How has investment portfolio pre-tax yield evolved from FY2022 through FY2024 across the six MI cohort issuers (MGIC, Radian, Essent, NMI, Enact, Arch)?

Here is the pre-tax investment yield evolution for each issuer based on their FY2024 10-Ks. Metrics and definitions differ slightly across companies — I note where comparability is limited.

| Issuer | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | Metric & basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MGIC (MTG)** | 3.0% | 3.7% | 4.0% | Pre-tax yield (implicit) |
| **Radian (RDN)** | 3.1% | 3.6% | 3.7% | Avg investment yield (MI subsidiaries, net investment income / avg invested assets at amortized cost) |
| **Essent (ESNT)** | n/a *(not located)* | 3.5% | 3.7% | Pre-tax investment income yield (based on amortized cost, excl. investment expenses) |
| **NMI (NMIH)** | n/a *(not located)* | n/a *(not located)* | 3.0% | Pre-tax book yield (net investment income / avg amortized cost) |
| **Enact (ACT)** | 3.1% | 3.6% | 4.0% | Pre-tax yield (% of avg investment portfolio assets) |
| **Arch (ACGL)** | n/a *(not located)* | 7.57% | 5.08% | Pre-tax **total return** on investments (before investment expenses) — *not a yield metric, not directly comparable* |

**Key takeaways:**
- **Trend:** Every issuer with FY2022 data shows a rising yield from FY2022 → FY2024 (MGIC: +100bp, Radian: +60bp, Enact: +90bp). This reflects the reinvestment of maturing low-coupon bonds into higher-rate securities.
- **Levels:** MGIC and Enact led at 4.0% in FY2024. Radian and Essent were close behind at 3.7%. NMI was notably lower at 3.0% (possibly reflecting a more conservative portfolio mix or shorter duration).
- **Arch Capital** reports a *total return* metric (including mark-to-market gains/losses and derivatives), not a running yield. Its 5.08% FY2024 total return is substantially lower than 7.57% in FY2023, reflecting the market impact of interest rate moves, but this is not a yield comparable to the other five.
- **Data gaps remain** for Essent's FY2022 yield and for NMI's FY2022 and FY2023 yields — those filings do not appear to disclose a pre-tax yield figure in the same way the FY2024 filing does.

Pull together everything Arch Capital disclosed about Q4 2024 share repurchases of its common stock — across the 10-K, the Q4 2024 8-K, and the Q4 2024 earnings call transcript. Are there discrepancies?

## Arch Capital Q4 2024 Share Repurchases — Three Sources Compared

### 10-K (FY 2024) — Item 5, Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities

| Period | Shares Purchased | Avg Price | Under Program | Program Remaining |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 2024 | 517 shares | $113.51 | — | $1,000.0M |
| Nov 2024 | 80 shares | $101.85 | — | $1,000.0M |
| Dec 2024 | 262,857 shares | $89.66 | 261,981 | $996.8M |
| **Q4 total** | **263,454** | **$89.71** | **261,981** | |

- 1,473 of the shares (517 + 80 + 876 of the Dec total) were employee tax-withholding repurchases, not under the program.
- The $1.0B authorization was newly approved by the Board on **December 20, 2024**, with no expiration.
- The Notes table (Share Repurchase Program) reports **$23.5M aggregate cost / 0.3M shares / $89.65 avg** for all program purchases in FY 2024.

### 8-K (Feb 10, 2025 — Q4 2024 Earnings Press Release)

**No mention of share repurchases.** The press release focuses on financial results, underwriting, investment income, and the special dividend — buybacks are not cited.

### Q4 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

**Prepared remarks** (Nicolas Papadopoulo):
> *"We also repurchased shares worth **$24 million** in the fourth quarter. Both the dividend and the share repurchase reflect our ongoing commitment to effective and active capital management."*

**Q&A** (Jimmy Bhullar → Francois Morin):
> *"I'm assuming part of the reason you did a little bit of buybacks this quarter versus none before was just the decline in the stock price…"*
> **Francois Morin:** *"For sure. I mean, it's something we look at regularly… in this particular situation, yes, there was opportunity in late in the fourth quarter."*

---

### Are there discrepancies?

**Essentially none. The three sources are consistent, with two caveats:**

1. **10-K vs. Transcript (rounding):** The 10-K shows ~$23.5M in program purchases for the year (essentially all Q4); the transcript rounds to **$24M**. That's the same number — no conflict.

2. **10-K Item 5 internal arithmetic:** 261,981 program shares at $89.66 implies a cost of ~$23.5M, yet the "remaining available" column drops by only **$3.2M** ($1,000M → $996.8M). This is explainable: the $1.0B authorization was brand new on **Dec 20**, so only the purchases made after that date (roughly the last 11 days of December) drew against the new program. The bulk of the December volume likely occurred before Dec 20 under a prior exhausted authorization. The table's footnote and the monthly-month structure don't break this out explicitly, which can look confusing, but there's no real discrepancy — the new program had barely been tapped by year-end.

3. **8-K omission:** The earnings press release doesn't mention buybacks at all, so it provides no cross-check. This is the only source that lacks the data; it doesn't create a contradiction with the other two.

If I want to spot which MI cohort issuer would be hit hardest by a new entrant disrupting pricing, what disclosures should I look at across the cohort, and what did the cohort actually say about pricing discipline in 2024?

**Disclosures to scrutinize** — These are the data points across the cohort that would signal vulnerability to a price-disrupting entrant: - **Risk-factor language on new entrants**: MGIC’s 2024 10-K explicitly warns that strong credit performance and high industry returns “may encourage new entrants … which could further increase competition.” Look for similar language in each issuer’s 10-K and whether any name a specific potential entrant (MGIC mentions “Anza Mortgage” as a possible 2026 entrant). - **Competitive position disclosures**: MGIC’s 10-K also notes that “pricing has become a key competitive factor” and that customers increasingly prioritize the lowest premium. An issuer with above-market premium yield or a weak market-share position in the most price-sensitive lender channels would be more exposed. - **Customer / lender concentration**: High concentration in any single lender or channel magnifies the risk of that lender defecting to a cheaper entrant. - **Premium yield trend**: A declining trend in new-business premium yield suggests the issuer is already having to cut price to win business, leaving less room to absorb further disruption. - **Expense ratio**: A higher expense ratio (e.g., G&A / net premiums earned) erodes the ability to match a new entrant’s lower price and still earn a target return. - **Reinsurance cost / structure**: If a new entrant is not using captive reinsurance (or uses less), it can undercut incumbents that have fixed cost-of-capital arrangements. - **PMIERs cushion / excess available assets**: A thinner cushion limits the ability to absorb a period of lower premiums while maintaining GSE eligibility, potentially forcing a defensive reaction. - **Dividend capacity and capital return**: Issuers that pay out a high proportion of earnings may need to cut dividends if margins compress, making them a riskier investment. --- **What the cohort actually said about pricing discipline in 2024** (all quotes from Q4 2024 earnings calls unless noted): | Company | Quote | |---------|-------| | **MGIC** | “We don’t talk a lot about sort of pricing dynamics … it feels like the risk return continues to be very favorable.” (Q4)
“It’s a competitive market … when we’re priced sort of more on par with the market and the risk-based, we’re probably going to get a little bit of outsized share.” (Q3) | | **Radian** | “The pricing environment continues to be rational and disciplined … you do see some movements here and there kind of around the edges … but overall, I would say the price environment continues to be stable.” (Q4)
“The pricing environment overall … has been pretty consistent really for probably the last 1.5 years to 2 years … continues to be rational and disciplined.” (Q3) | | **Essent** | “Our industry remains competitive and strong credit guardrails remain in place … we are pleased with our position in the marketplace and the unit economics that we are achieving on new business.” (Q4) | | **NMI** | “The MI pricing environment remains balanced and constructive as well, allowing us to fully and fairly support our lenders and their borrowers, while at the same time appropriately protect risk adjusted returns.” (Q4)
“Industry pricing is generally stable and, we would say, rational. We’re really encouraged by the discipline that we see across the market.” (Q3) | | **Enact** | “Pricing remained constructive in the quarter, and we maintained our commitment to prudent underwriting standards.” (Q4)
“MI pricing continues to be competitive, but also expected pricing returns … continue to remain attractive within our risk-adjusted return appetite … we generally see pricing as constructive in the market.” (Q3) | **Summary of the tone**: Every major MI issuer described pricing as “rational,” “disciplined,” “stable,” or “constructive” throughout 2024. None reported a price war. The risk of a new entrant was cited only by MGIC in its 10-K risk factors, not on any call. The cohort believes the current equilibrium will persist, but the upfront risk-factor disclosure from MGIC (and the absence of it from peers) is itself a red flag to watch — especially if the “Anza Mortgage” 2026 entry materializes.
